title: Constraints shared by ZIA Terraform rule resources: order and predefined rules
aliases: terraform rule order must be positive

prose.text: Rule-based ZIA resources share order and predefined-rule constraints. {{order-positive-integer}} What a non-positive order does at the API is open {{gap:nonpositive-order-effect}}.

prose.label: Order.
prose.text: {{order-contiguous}} How orders are applied and what can go wrong: [[zia.terraform.rule-order]].

checks.do: Whether configured orders start at 1 and have no gaps, including after a custom rule was deleted.
Whether a failed destroy was a predefined rule that the provider refuses to delete.

order-positive-integer.statement: The `zia_dlp_web_rules` documentation says `order` must always be a positive whole number starting at 1, with negative numbers and zero unsupported and an error, and the `zia_url_filtering_rules` and `zia_firewall_filtering_rules` schemas validate it with `IntAtLeast(1)`.

quotes: The `order` attribute must always be a positive whole number starting at 1.
ValidateFunc: validation.IntAtLeast(1),
ValidateFunc: validation.IntAtLeast(1),

order-contiguous.statement: The provider documents that rule orders must be contiguous with no gaps. Up to v4.8.13 its page said deleting a rule must be followed by renumbering the remaining rules so the API honours the order; from v4.8.14 it says to renumber the remaining rules so the orders stay contiguous, and that the deletion and the renumbering can be applied together in one `terraform apply`.

quotes: Rule orders must always be contiguous (no gaps).
When you delete a rule, renumber the remaining rules so the orders stay contiguous.
the deletion and the renumbering can be applied together in one `terraform apply`
Rule orders must always be contiguous (no gaps).
Deleting a rule must be followed by order number re-adjustment of the remaining rules to ensure the API honours the required order.

predefined-reorder-not-destroy.statement: Predefined rules can be managed through the provider for reordering, but destroy is not supported for them and not every attribute of a custom rule applies. Up to v4.8.13 the rule page also said to delete a custom rule with `-target`; the v4.8.14 changelog says deleting the rule with `-target` first is no longer needed.

quotes: Predefined rules can be managed via the Terraform provider for reordering purposes; however, `destroy` operations are not supported for predefined rules, and not all attributes available on custom rules apply to them.
When deleting existing custom rules, use the Terraform `-target` flag to target the specific rule to be removed.
deleting the rule with `-target` first is no longer needed

upstream.note: The `-target` delete workaround is no longer needed from provider v4.8.14 (PR 614).

firewall-predefined-ordering-automatic.statement: For firewall filtering rules the documentation says predefined rules cannot be deleted and the provider reorders around them.

quotes: Zscaler Cloud Firewall contain default and predefined rules which cannot be deleted (not all attributes are supported on predefined rules).
Handle reordering around predefined rules

firewall-predefined-delete-errors.statement: Deleting a predefined firewall filtering rule through the provider returns an error, both for a fixed list of predefined rule names and for any rule whose `predefined` flag is set.

firewall-predefined-import-then-destroy-.statement: A predefined firewall rule can be imported into state, but `terraform destroy` then fails; the documented route is to remove the rules you want to delete and re-run `terraform apply`.

quotes: The import of `predefined` rules is still possible in case you want o have them under the Terraform management; however, remember that these rules cannot be deleted.
the provider will fail when executing `terraform destroy`; hence, you must remove the rules you want to delete, and re-run `terraform apply` instead.

nonpositive-order-effect.title: Whether a zero or negative order can reach ZIA and create undeletable internal rules
nonpositive-order-effect.blocks: saying that a non-positive order creates undeletable rules
nonpositive-order-effect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: a legacy catalog said negative or zero values create undeletable internal rules; the provider docs say they are unsupported and an error, and the schema rejects them at plan time. Whether the API itself would accept such an order is not shown.
